title: Clothing and material Jelly sent the girls
summary: He sent cloth for skirts and coats from Vancouver; grandmother's sacrifices for school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, let's see, now again, is there anything else that your brother ever sent you that you can remember? Or did he...
I mean, I can remember everything he ever sent me, but I mean, I don't have anything to show as a woman, because I'm not...
No, I don't have anything to show as a woman, because I'm not...

No, I don't have anything to show as a woman, because I'm not... No, I mean, now you see, we had to wear blue skirts at the school. And he would send the material to make the skirts. Mm-hmm. And they didn't want us to wear embroidered blouses, and he just wouldn't get that, and he said that we had to have plain white blouses. And my grandmother would always have to make his dresses. Our Sunday dresses were made out of material he sent for the blouses.
But he'd pick out the material and send it to you. He'd send the material, and he'd send... He'd send the material, and he'd send... Vancouver, that's what I'm trying to...

Oh, Vancouver. He was up to... He'd send us some things from Vancouver, and my goodness, my grandmother, they were too large for us anyway. He must have thought we were going to be bean balls, like him. But he'd send coats and sweaters, and I mean, little coats here, and weren't supposed to wear the kind of coats he was sending us. Yeah. And sometimes she'd let us go to school with him, and sometimes she wouldn't. Mm-hmm. She said, because when I'm not able to pay that fifty cents a week for you to go to school, the sisters would look over here and feed you all and everything. When Chad asked me, you know, she didn't... She wouldn't let us stay down there until the weekend. Yeah. And I was so glad to stay in school all the time. Mm-hmm. Because when I'd come home, we had so many babies to take care of. Yeah. We might have so many children.

I tried to give my son the same opportunity that I had, even after... Because my grandmother left no stones in turn where we were concerned. Yeah. I'd see her cry many days. Yeah. And wouldn't tell us what she was crying about, but she wanted us to have everything that every other child had. Yeah.
